Most People Wait Too Long

Pain shows up differently at every age. Most people ignore the early signs until it’s much harder to reverse.

Here is what your body is most
vulnerable to and when.

20s

Posture problems begin

Tech neck, wrist strain and poor desk habits start building the foundation for chronic pain.

30s

The decade it shows up

Lower back pain, knee issues and repetitive strain become hard to ignore for the first time.

40s

Compensation kicks in

Your body starts compensating for old injuries. What feels manageable starts limiting how you move.

50s+

Chronic becomes daily

Arthritis, spondylosis and joint degeneration peak. By then, lasting damage is harder to reverse.

Catch the Signs Early

Find out how your musculoskeletal health is doing before small issues become chronic problems.

The Physio Edge Course

Master preventive pain care and join India’s most trusted network of certified physiotherapists. Learn from experts, get certified, get featured, get discovered.

About This Certification Course

The betterhood Physio Certification is designed for physiotherapists who want to specialize in preventive pain care and musculoskeletal wellness. Beyond traditional physiotherapy education, this course combines scientific evidence with practical protocols while also teaching communication mastery and the business mindset needed to build a successful career and loyal clientele.

Course Curriculum

Module 1: Posture As A Living System

Learn to see posture not as a fixed alignment but as the body’s intelligent survival strategy. Understand how gravity, fatigue, and body mechanics shape posture throughout the day.

Module 2: Mental Health, Emotion & Posture

Discover how emotions, stress, and the nervous system influence posture and pain patterns. Learn to identify emotional signals in the body and use posture to help regulate mood and recovery.

Module 3: Environment, Lifestyle & Posture Ecosystem

Understand how everyday habits like workspaces, sleep, footwear, and travel shape posture. Learn how to redesign your patient’s environment to support long-term recovery.

Module 4: Art of Non-Technical Posture Assessment

Train your clinical eye to read the body beyond textbook assessments. Learn how to detect patterns through observation, breath, movement, and subtle physical cues.

Module 5: Recovery, Fatigue & Postural Resilience

Learn how fatigue, recovery, and the nervous system influence posture and injury risk. Understand the recovery pyramid and how to build resilient bodies that sustain performance.

Module 6: The Real World Physio Mindset

Go beyond technical skills to build trust, authority, and a successful physiotherapy career. Learn communication, patient psychology, and the mindset required to thrive in real practice.

Module Structure

Each module is broken down into 4 key components:

  • Video Content: 5 short instructional videos per module
  • Text Content: Comprehensive reading materials and study guides
  • Tools: Practical tools and templates (provided as per module requirements)
  • Assessment: 1 final module assessment

  • Employees are expected to adhere to the policy and report any violations promptly to HR or the designated officer.
  1. Grievance Procedure
  • Any employee who believes they have been subjected to discrimination or harassment should report the matter immediately to the HR department or designated Grievance Officer.
  • Complaints will be investigated promptly and confidentially. Appropriate corrective measures will be taken.
  1. Enforcement and Consequences
  • Violations of this policy may lead to disciplinary action, including termination of employment.
  • No retaliation will be tolerated against employees who report discrimination in good faith.
  1. Legal Compliance
  • This policy complies with the Indian Constitution Articles 15 and 16, Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 and other applicable laws.
  1. Communication and Review
  • This policy will be communicated to all employees during onboarding and periodically thereafter.
  • The policy will be reviewed and updated as necessary to comply with changes in legal requirements and company standards.

Violations and Reporting

  • Violations of this policy, regardless of whether an actual law has been violated will not be tolerated.
  • The Company will promptly, thoroughly and fairly investigate every issue that is brought to its attention in this area and will take disciplinary action, when appropriate, up to and including termination of employment.
  • Employees who believe they have been subjected to discrimination, harassment, or any violation of this policy are encouraged to report the matter immediately.
  • Reports can be made without fear of retaliation or victimization.
  • All complaints will be treated confidentially to the extent possible and investigated impartially.

Reporting Violations

For any questions, concerns, or to report suspected breaches regarding this policy, please contact our Grievance Officer:

Return Policy

  1. Return Window

Customers can request a return, replacement, or exchange within 7 days of delivery.

To be eligible for a return:

  • The product should be in good condition.
  • The product should include original packaging where possible.
  • The product should not show signs of heavy use, damage, stains, or misuse.

Returned products will be inspected before processing refunds or exchanges.

  1. Free Size Exchange

For support products such as Back Support, Knee Support, Elbow Support, Wrist Support, and other braces, betterhood offers one free size exchange if the product does not fit properly.

Customers may try the product for fit and comfort, but the product should not show excessive wear or damage.

  1. Damaged, Defective, or Incorrect Product

If you receive a product that is:

  • Damaged during delivery
  • Defective
  • Incorrect item delivered

Please contact our support team within 48 hours of delivery.

After verification, our team will arrange a free replacement or refund.

Customers may be asked to share photos of the product and packaging for verification.

  1. Non-Returnable Products

For hygiene and safety reasons, certain products cannot be returned once opened unless they are damaged or defective.

These include:

  • Roll-ons, patches, lotions, creams, and other topical-use products
  • Products showing heavy usage, stains, or physical damage
  1. How to Request a Return or Exchange

To request a return or exchange, please contact our support team and provide the following details:

  • Order ID
  • Product name
  • Reason for return or exchange

Customers may be required to share product images or videos for verification before return approval.  Pickup will typically be arranged within 2–3 working days after approval.

  1. Return Shipping

Free return pickup will be provided in the following cases:

  • Damaged product
  • Incorrect product delivered
  • Approved size exchange

If a return is requested due to personal preference, change of mind, or an order placed by mistake, a nominal return fee may apply. This fee can vary based on location and logistics, and will be clearly communicated during the return approval process.

To make things easy, betterhood can arrange a doorstep pickup for you. The applicable return fee will be adjusted against your refund.

Alternatively, if you prefer, you may also choose to self-ship the product to our return address. Once we receive and verify the product, your return will be processed smoothly.

Repeated returns or misuse of the return policy may result in restrictions on future orders or returns.

  1. Refund Policy

Once the returned product is received and inspected, refunds will be processed.

  • Refunds are initiated within 5–7 business days after inspection.
  • Refunds will be credited to the original payment method used during purchase.

Depending on the bank or payment provider, it may take additional time for the amount to reflect in the account.  

  1. Cancellation Policy

Orders can be cancelled only before they are dispatched.

Once the order has been shipped, cancellation will no longer be possible. Customers may refuse the delivery or request a return after receiving the order.

  1. Customer Support

For any queries related to returns, replacements, or refunds, please contact our support team.

Email: care@betterhood.in

Phone no :-  +918484805885

Aging

As age progresses, the natural degeneration of cartilage and bones can weaken joints and muscles, leading to conditions like osteoarthritis. This deterioration often results in chronic pain, reduced mobility, and increased vulnerability to injuries.

Occupational factors like repetitive motions, heavy lifting, and prolonged sitting can strain muscles and joints, leading to wear and tear over time. This strain often results in chronic pain and increases the risk of developing musculoskeletal disorders.

Smoking impairs blood flow and reduces the delivery of essential nutrients to muscles, bones, and joints, accelerating degeneration and increasing the risk of chronic pain. It also weakens the immune system, making it harder for the body to repair damaged tissues and exacerbating joint inflammation.

Genetic factors, including predispositions to cancer, certain neurological and autoimmune conditions, skeletal deformities, and gastrointestinal disorders, can negatively impact muscle, bone, and joint health. These conditions can lead to chronic pain by causing inflammation, nerve damage, or altering the body’s ability to repair tissues effectively.

Obesity places excessive stress on muscles, bones, and joints, particularly in weight-bearing areas like the knees and hips, leading to accelerated wear and tear. This added strain contributes to joint pain and increases the risk of developing chronic conditions like osteoarthritis.

Diabetes disrupts blood circulation and impedes healing, which can weaken muscles and deteriorate joint health. Persistent high blood sugar levels exacerbate inflammation and nerve damage, often resulting in chronic pain and stiffness.

Assess your Knee Health

Hey there! This health assessment tool is designed by our experts. We will guide you through a series of movements and ask you to report your observations. These movements are carefully curated to assess various key aspects of your musculoskeletal health. Some of them will need to be performed lying on the ground or sitting on a chair/stool. For certain movements, you will need to record the time, and the timer on your mobile device can be helpful for this.
Based on your responses, this assessment tool will generate your health score on a scale of 1 to 10. When taken periodically, this health score will help you monitor your health progress. So, find a quiet corner, and let’s get started.

Please note that your information shared here is completely safe and is used only for arriving at the assessment results. The assessment results are indicative and do not substitute medical expert consultation in any way. Appropriate user discretion is advised. You may refer to our Terms of Service for further clarity.

Lying leg raise

1. Get into the position and record the time for which you can stay in the position. Complete the test on both sides. Record your lowest score of the two.(Required)

How to test?

Lie face down with your legs straight and arms at your sides. Gradually, lift one leg off the ground while keeping it straight. Repeat on other side.

Did You Know?

The knee joint carres up to five times the body's weight during activities like running and jumping, making it one of the most heavily loaded joints in the body.

Single leg balance

2. Get into the position and record the time for which you can stay in the position. Complete the test on both sides. Record your lowest score of the two.(Required)

How to test?

Stand on one leg with your knee slightly bent and arms crossed over your chest. Hold the position as long as possible without losing balance, then switch legs.

Did You Know?

Our joints are all connected, like a game of dominos! When there’s a problem in the knee, it can tip the balance and lead to back pain, proving just how intertwined our body’s mechanics really are.

Knee flexion

3. Select the position you can perform without changing your pain or discomfort.(Required)

How to test?

Stand or sit with your back straight. Gradually, bend one knee to lift your heel toward your buttocks. Repeat on other side.

Did You Know?

Sitting for long periods can lead to tight hamstrings, pulling on the knee joint and causing pain—proof that staying active is key to keeping your knees happy!

This field is hidden when viewing the form
This field is hidden when viewing the form

Knee internal rotation

4. Select the position you can perform without changing your pain or discomfort.(Required)

How to test?

Sit with your knee bent at 90 degrees. Gradually rotate your lower leg inward while keeping your knee in place.

Did You Know?

The patella, or kneecap, is a floating plate that glides over the knee joint, supported by muscles; tight thigh muscles can pull on the patella, causing friction and leading to knee problems.

Knee external rotation

5. Select the position you can perform without changing your pain or discomfort.(Required)

How to test?

Sit with your knee bent at 90 degrees. Gradually rotate your lower leg outward while keeping your knee in place.

Did You Know?

Flat feet can lead to knee issues by altering your gait and putting extra stress on the knees, showcasing how foot structure plays a crucial role in overall joint health!

Hey there! This health assessment tool is designed by our experts. We will guide you through a series of movements and ask you to report your observations. These movements are carefully curated to assess various key aspects of your musculoskeletal health. Some of them will need to be performed lying on the ground or sitting on a chair/stool. Pike planks duration

1. Get into the position and record the time for which you can stay in the position.(Required)

How to test?

Start in a plank position with hands under your shoulders and feet together. Lift your hips toward the ceiling, forming an inverted "V".

Did You Know?

Pike planks are a powerful indicator of shoulder strength, as they engage the deltoids and stabilize the shoulder joint while challenging core stability and control.

This field is hidden when viewing the form

2. When you pull your arm down gently (as if someone is pulling it straight down), do you notice any of the following? Please select the option that best describes your experience:(Required)

How to test?

Start in a plank position with hands under your shoulders and feet together. Lift your hips toward the ceiling, forming an inverted "V".

Did You Know?

The shoulder is the most unstable joint in the body due to its shallow socket and wide range of motion, making it susceptible to dislocations and injuries despite its incredible flexibility.

This field is hidden when viewing the form
This field is hidden when viewing the form

Shoulder flexion

3. Select the position you can perform without changing your pain or discomfort. Complete the test on both sides. Record your lowest score of the two.(Required)

How to test?

Stand or sit with a straight back and arms at your sides. Gradually raise your arms straight in front of youas high as they can go, keeping them straight. Repeat on other side.

Did You Know?

The shoulder is the most mobile joint in the body, offering an extraordinary range of motion that facilitates diverse movements like lifting, throwing, and reaching overhead.

This field is hidden when viewing the form
This field is hidden when viewing the form

Shoulder abduction

4. Select the position you can perform without changing your pain or discomfort. Complete the test on both sides. Record your lowest score of the two.(Required)

How to test?

Stand or sit with a straight back and arms at your sides. Gradually raise your arms out to the sides as high as they can comfortably go. Repeat on other side.

Did You Know?

Frozen shoulder, or adhesive capsulitis, is a painful condition that limits overhead movement, often occurring after an injury or long periods of immobility.

This field is hidden when viewing the form

Cross body adduction

5. Select the position you can perform without changing your pain or discomfort. Complete the test on both sides. Record your lowest score of the two.(Required)

How to test?

Stand or sit with a straight back and arms at your sides. Gradually bring one arm across your body behind your back toward the opposite shoulder. Repeat on other side.

Did You Know?

Tennis elbow, or lateral epicondylitis, is a painful condition caused by inflammation of the outer elbow tendons, often due to repetitive wrist and arm movements, affecting even non-tennis players.

This field is hidden when viewing the form

Shoulder external rotation

6. Select the position you can perform without changing your pain or discomfort. Complete the test on both sides. Record your lowest score of the two.(Required)

How to test?

Stand or sit with your elbows bent at 90 degrees and arms close to your body. Gradually rotate your forearms outward, keeping your elbows stationary. Repeat on other side.

Did You Know?

Shoulder rotator cuff tears are surprisingly common, affecting about one in five people over the age of 50, and can result from wear and tear rather than just injury, making shoulder health a crucial focus as we age!

The shoulder can bear an impressive load, capable of handling up to three times the body’s weight during activities like lifting or throwing, showcasing its strength and versatility!

Shoulder dislocations are the most common joint dislocations, often occurring during sports or falls.

Step 1 of 9

11%

Assess your Back Health

Hey there! This health assessment tool is designed by our experts. We will guide you through a series of movements and ask you to report your observations. These movements are carefully curated to assess various key aspects of your musculoskeletal health. Some of them will need to be performed lying on the ground or sitting on a chair/stool. For certain movements, you will need to record the time, and the timer on your mobile device can be helpful for this.
Based on your responses, this assessment tool will generate your health score on a scale of 1 to 10. When taken periodically, this health score will help you monitor your health progress. So, find a quiet corner, and let’s get started.

Please note that your information shared here is completely safe and is used only for arriving at the assessment results. The assessment results are indicative and do not substitute medical expert consultation in any way. Appropriate user discretion is advised. You may refer to our Terms of Service for further clarity.

Superman duration

1. Get into the position and record the time for which you can stay in the position.(Required)

How to test?

Lie face down with arms extended in front and legs straight. Engage your core, then lift your arms, chest, and legs off the ground simultaneously

Did You Know?

The Superman duration is a great indicator of lower back strength because it engages the entire posterior chain, highlighting the stability and strength of the lower back muscles.

This field is hidden when viewing the form
This field is hidden when viewing the form
This field is hidden when viewing the form

Bird dog duration

2. Get into the position and record the time for which you can stay in the position. Complete the test on both sides. Record your lowest score of the two.(Required)

How to test?

Start on all fours and extend one arm forward and the opposite leg back while keeping your back flat. Repeat on other side.

Did You Know?

The bird dog duration is an excellent indicator of balance as it engages core stability and tests the coordination between the upper and lower body.

This field is hidden when viewing the form

Slump Test

3. Perform the movement as described here. Indicate the change of pain or discomfort when performing the movement.(Required)

How to test?

Sit at the edge of a chair, slouch forward, and extend one leg straight with a flexed foot. Note any pain or tightness in your back or legs.

Did You Know?

The slump test is a valuable tool for assessing back mobility as it evaluates the flexibility of the spine and the nervous system under tension, helping identify potential issues.

Lying leg drop

4. Perfom the movement as described here. Indicate the change of pain or discomfort when performing the movement.(Required)

How to test?

Lie on your back with knees bent. Drop your knees to one side, keeping your shoulders down, then switch sides. Note any pain or tightness in your back or legs.

Did You Know?

Range of motion (ROM) measures how far a joint can move in various directions, serving as a key indicator of overall muscle, bone, and joint health.

5. Select the position you can perform without changing your pain or discomfort.(Required)

How to test?

Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and arms crossed over your chest. Then gradually bend to one side, keeping your back straight. Repeat on other side.

Did You Know?

The maximum lateral flexion (side bending) of the spine varies by individual but can reach approximately 35 degrees.

Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and arms crossed over your chest. Rotate your torso to one side gradually. Repeat on other side.

Did You Know?

The spine's unique structure, comprising adaptable vertebrae and intervertebral discs, provides the lower back with crucial stability and support, while the upper back offers impressive flexibility, allowing for about 30 degrees of rotation.

Spinal flexion is supported by intervertebral discs, which act as shock absorbers, allowing the spine to bend while protecting against injury.

Smoking impairs blood flow and reduces the delivery of essential nutrients to muscles, bones, and joints, accelerating degeneration and increasing the risk of chronic pain. As age progresses, the natural degeneration of cartilage and bones can weaken joints and muscles, leading to conditions like osteoarthritis. This deterioration often results in chronic pain, reduced mobility, and increased vulnerability to injuries.

Occupational factors like repetitive motions, heavy lifting, and prolonged sitting can strain muscles and joints, leading to wear and tear over time. This strain often results in chronic pain and increases the risk of developing musculoskeletal disorders.

Smoking impairs blood flow and reduces the delivery of essential nutrients to muscles, bones, and joints, accelerating degeneration and increasing the risk of chronic pain. It also weakens the immune system, making it harder for the body to repair damaged tissues and exacerbating joint inflammation.

Genetic factors, including predispositions to cancer, certain neurological and autoimmune conditions, skeletal deformities, and gastrointestinal disorders, can negatively impact muscle, bone, and joint health. These conditions can lead to chronic pain by causing inflammation, nerve damage, or altering the body’s ability to repair tissues effectively.

Obesity places excessive stress on muscles, bones, and joints, particularly in weight-bearing areas like the knees and hips, leading to accelerated wear and tear. This added strain contributes to joint pain and increases the risk of developing chronic conditions like osteoarthritis.

Diabetes disrupts blood circulation and impedes healing, which can weaken muscles and deteriorate joint health. Persistent high blood sugar levels exacerbate inflammation and nerve damage, often resulting in chronic pain and stiffness.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I know whether betterhood<sup class="ctm">TM</sup> is for me?

betterhoodTM is for anyone looking to improve health, prevent age-related decline, and enhance well-being. If you want science-backed, personalized care to age healthily, betterhoodTM is a great fit. Remember, age-related decline can begin in your 30s, so it’s crucial to incorporate preventive measures early.

What health concerns does betterhood<sup class="ctm">TM</sup> address?

betterhoodTM addresses a range of health concerns related to aging, including musculoskeletal health, posture, recovery, nutrition, fitness, and joint health, all through scientifically proven solutions.

Where can I access betterhood<sup class="ctm">TM</sup>'s educative resources?

betterhoodTM‘s educative resources are available through the ‘Learn’ section hosted on our website, and on our Instagram and YouTube channels. These include articles, videos, expert webinars, and guides on topics related to healthy aging, fitness, and nutrition.

Does betterhood<sup class="ctm">TM</sup> offer only products?

No, betterhoodTM offers a holistic approach, including personalized health assessments, fitness plans, nutritional guidance, and educational resources. We offer both products and services aimed at improving your health span.

How do I know whether betterhood<sup class="ctm">TM</sup> recommendations are working?

You can track progress through regular health assessments hosted in the ‘betterYou corner’ section hosted on our website. These health assessments help you track your key musculoskeletal health metrics like posture, strength, mobility, balance and overall well-being. We provide tools to monitor your health over time.

How do betterhood<sup class="ctm">TM</sup>'s diagnostic assessments work?

betterhoodTM ‘s diagnostic assessments provide a comprehensive evaluation of back, neck, shoulder, and knee pain through clinically designed questions. These questions help record symptoms for differential diagnosis. While the results are preliminary and may require further evaluation, they are typically sufficient to create personalized care plans and track progress.

How do betterhood<sup class="ctm">TM</sup> health assessments work?

betterhoodTM‘s health assessments combine physical tests and lifestyle evaluations to analyze your current health status. Physical tests assess range of motion and ease of movement to evaluate mobility, as well as hold durations in certain positions to assess balance and strength. Based on the results, we provide tailored recommendations and actionable steps to improve your well-being.

What is the longevity goal-setting offered by betterhood<sup class="ctm">TM</sup>, and how does it work?

betterhoodTM’s longevity goal-setting helps you set personalized health goals based on the life you envision in your 80s. Your desired lifestyle at that age determines the health and fitness levels to aim for now. You can set your health score targets based on your longevity goals and track your progress.

What is the Centenarian Challenge?

The Centenarian Challenge is an initiative by betterhoodTM to encourage individuals to adopt healthy habits with the goal of living a vibrant, active life well into their 100s. It involves setting lifestyle goals based on longevity science to promote physical, mental, and emotional well-being.

Our Story

Why do we age? Are chronic pain and cognitive decline inevitable, or can we influence the aging process? We noticed these issues in our parents and saw signs of aging appearing in ourselves as early as in our 30s.

While research in longevity and physiotherapy offers solutions to extend healthspan, current practices often focus on treatment only after issues arise. We are building ‘betterhood’ with the aim to fill this gap with a holistic, age-tailored approach, striving to become India’s most comprehensive pain-care ecosystem.

– Neha & Vikram

Our Team

Our team is driven by a shared mission to help India age better and healthier. We are deeply concerned about how aging is viewed in our society and believe that many age-related issues can be addressed and managed through science. Aging should be treated as a condition that can be improved, not just a natural decline. This shift in perspective can only happen through open, positive conversations and a deeper understanding of our bodies. We are passionate about leading this change and empowering individuals to take control of their health as they age.

Our Expert

Shayamal Vallabhjee
Chief Science Officer, betterhood
Performance Psychologist | Sports Scientist

Shayamal Vallabhjee is a Performance Psychologist, Coach, and Sports Scientist with deep expertise in team dynamics and personality. With over 20 years of experience, he has worked with elite athletes, Fortune 500 executives, and championship teams, helping them optimise mindset, communication, and performance.

He serves as faculty at Stanford Business School’s LEAD Program and advises leading sports tech brands and global organisations. Known for his powerful workshops and keynotes delivered across 1,000+ stages worldwide, Shayamal combines evidence-based sports science with cognitive behavioural science and spiritual insight to drive meaningful and lasting change.

We adhere strictly to scientifically proven and tested methods, ensuring only effective, evidence-based health solutions.

Wellness

Personalized Health Care

Our approach tailors treatments and plans to meet the unique needs of each individual. Effectiveness is in personalization.

Empathy and Understanding

We listen to our customers and continuously refine our products. We believe that improvement is an ongoing process.
